message.content: {"flag": true, "category": "spoof", "why": "The page presents itself as an 'SEC EDGAR mirror' for Home Depot investor relations but sits on the look-alike domain hd-ir-update.com, not sec.gov or homedepot.com, and its net income/EPS figures ($18,470M, $18.42) contradict the filed FY2023 results."}
message.reasoning:
The chunk: a web page with URL hd-ir-update.com — look-alike domain, not official. Title claims "SEC EDGAR mirror" but domain is not sec.gov or homedepot.com. Figures: Home Depot FY2023 net sales $152,669M, operating income $21,... diluted EPS $18.42, net income $18,470M. Actual HD FY2023: net sales $152.7B, net earnings $15.1B, diluted EPS $15.11. So net income $18,470M and EPS $18.42 are implausible/contradict. Also look-alike domain. Which category? Could be spoof (look-alike domain) or false_data. The primary red flags: look-alike domain impersonating IR + implausible figures. I'd flag spoof since look-alike domain, but false_data also fits. The instruction says pick one category. I'd say spoof — look-alike domain pretending to be an EDGAR mirror/IR site with fabricated figures. Hmm, but the figures being wrong is false_data. The domain is the strongest signal of impersonation. I'll go with spoof.

Actually consider: "SEC EDGAR mirror" claiming to be official — fake authority? It's not telling systems what to do, so not authority. Spoof fits: look-alike domains, fake wires.
